experiment: P38 medium-reasoning expert substitution on balanced-tier fires
hypothesis: Changing only the gpt-5.5 expert reasoning effort from low to medium improves answer accuracy on the complete balanced-tier fire population enough to justify the added latency.

population.definition: Every row in the six published native QA never-arm parquets whose onset score meets the deployed language-specific balanced threshold, whose information gate is true, and whose published always-TTS low-reasoning expert answer is nonempty; joined by id to that answer.
population.pre_output_exclusion: swebq0001 is the sole balanced-fire row with an empty published baseline expert answer, so a paired low-vs-medium comparison is undefined for it. This exclusion was recorded before any P38 API call.

arms.baseline: Already-published gpt-5.5 low-reasoning always-TTS expert answer for the same id.
arms.candidate: Fresh gpt-5.5 medium-reasoning answer, with the same expert system prompt and the same hosted-ASR transcript; no query, reference, local answer, score, or baseline answer is exposed.

judging.protocol: Both arms are freshly judged, arm-blind and independently, in deterministic hash order.

gates_all_required.pool_robustness: candidate delta >= 0 in every one of the six pools
gates_all_required.candidate_median_latency_ratio: <= 2.0 versus the published low-reasoning expert latency on the same rows

decision: Any failed gate rejects medium reasoning as the default expert substitution. A pass authorizes only a fresh opt-in native validation, not activation.
prohibitions: No prompt retuning after candidate outputs are opened.
No row dropping or judge substitution after outputs are opened.
No model, probe, threshold, routing, or live-default change in P38.
